full_judgment: 2. The appellant lodged a First Information Report with the Kachua Police Station against respondent No. 2 alleging that the latter had stolen away his tractor whereupon a Criminal Case being Case No. 125 of 1974 was started in the Court of Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Chandpur and tractor was seized from his possession. The magistrate made over the tractor to the custody of the appellant who executed a bond to the effect that he would produce the tractor before the Court whenever called for and in case of failure to do so, would pay Tk. 80,000/-. On conclusion of enquiry in that Case respondent No.2 was discharged as no prima facie case of theft was made out and on his application the Magistrate directed the appellant to produce the tractor for ultimate delivery to the respondent. On receipt of the notice, the appellant appeared before the Magistrate and took several adjournments taking various pleas including the plea that for determination of ownership of the tractor a civil suit was pending and as such production of the tractor should be deferred till disposal of the suit. The suit in fact was filed not by the appellant but was filed by respondent No. 2 for a declaration that he was entitled to take deli very of the tractor. The suit was decreed, but the appellant challenged the decree by an appeal before the High Court Division. In that appeal, he made an application for a temporary injunction to restrain the respondent, plaintiff of the suit, from taking delivery of the tractor from the Magistrate. But the application was dismissed and temporary injunction was refused. The Magistrate then directed the appellant to produce the tractor before the Officer-in- Charge of the Kachua Police Station and, on the appellant's failure to produce the tractor, started a criminal proceeding under section 406 of the Penal Code, being G.R. Case No 51 of 1978 and issued process against him for criminal breach of trust.
